summary.oneLiner: VBL delivered a robust Q1CY26 with 16.3% volume growth and 55bps EBITDA margin expansion, driven by strong summer demand, operational efficiencies from new large-scale plants, and successful international M&A (Twizza), effectively neutralizing marginal realization declines and input cost headwinds through inventory hedging and discount rationalization.

one-line thesis: VBL delivered a robust Q1CY26 with 16.3% volume growth and 55bps EBITDA margin expansion, driven by strong summer demand, operational efficiencies from new large-scale plants, and successful international M&A (Twizza), effectively neutralizing marginal realization declines and input cost headwinds through inventory hedging and discount rationalization.
financial scorecard: Revenue: Rs. 65,742 mn (+18.1% YoY); EBITDA: Rs. 15,289 mn (+21% YoY), Margin 23.3% (+55bps YoY); PAT: Rs. 8,787 mn (+20.1% YoY); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but finance costs up 18% due to Twizza acquisition; One-offs: Higher depreciation (+30.9%) from 4 new plants commissioned last year; Higher finance costs from ZAR-denominated debt for Twizza.
guidance: Revenue Growth: Confident in sustained double-digit growth (5-10 year horizon); Margin: Expect efficiencies to offset input inflation; Capex: Reduced to <Rs. 500-600 crore for India in CY26 (only 1 new plant planned) due to sufficient capacity; Commissioning: New plants (Buxar, Prayagraj, Damtal, Meghalaya) stabilized and driving efficiency.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Demand visibility high due to 6-month raw material inventory cover and strong summer trends; Distribution expansion target: ~500,000 new outlets in CY26.
segment / subsidiary detail: CSD: 73.6% of volumes; NCB: 7.5%; Water: 18.9%; Low/No-sugar mix: ~63% of total volume; India Volume: +14.4%; International Volume: +21.4% (broad-based across Africa, not just SA); Dairy segment growing 60-70%; Energy drinks (Sting, Ad-Rush) seeing strong demand, constrained by can shortage.
growth verticals / optionality: International expansion (Africa snacks & dairy); Portfolio diversification (Energy, Juice, Dairy); Route-to-market density (adding 300k-500k outlets/year); Upsizing packs (250ml to 400ml) driving liter growth; New product launches (Sting Classic, Adrenaline Rush Rs. 60 SKU).
margins & cost dynamics: Gross Margin: 55.2% (+62bps YoY) due to early raw material stocking; EBITDA Margin: 23.3% (+55bps YoY); India EBITDA Margin: +112bps; Cost pressures: Packaging (PET, Aluminum cans) and transportation due to oil/geopolitics; Mitigation: 6-month inventory cover (Intl), partial cover (India), discount reduction, operational leverage from new high-speed plants.
capex / expansion: CY26 India Capex guidance: <Rs. 500-600 crore (low vs historical due to capacity sufficiency); Focus shifted to M&A (Twizza: ZAR 2,053 mn EV; Crickley Dairy: ZAR 238 mn EV) rather than greenfield; New plants utilize 1,000 bpm lines vs old 200 bpm, improving RoCE (~30%) and payback (3-4 years).
capital allocation: Interim dividend approved: 25% of face value (Rs. 0.50/share), total outflow ~Rs. 1,691 mn; M&A focused on Africa (Twizza closed, Crickley pending) to broaden portfolio and utilize existing capacity; Disciplined working capital management.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical tension impacting crude/oil prices (transportation & packaging costs); Unseasonal weather (rains) disrupting summer sales; Aluminum can shortage constraining energy drink volumes; Intense competition (Campa, Coke) leading to potential price wars; Currency fluctuation in African markets.
management quality / tone: Confident and bullish on long-term structural growth (double-digit for 5-10 years); Pragmatic on near-term inflation (hedged, but monitoring); Aggressive on distribution expansion and market share gains; Emphasizes operational efficiency and scale advantages over competitors.
non-obvious takeaways: Management claims 6-month raw material inventory in international markets (vs industry norm of much less), providing a significant competitive cost advantage during inflation; Shift from greenfield capex to M&A in Africa indicates a strategy to instantly acquire capacity and route-to-market rather than build; Realization decline in India (-1.5%) is improving sequentially (-4% in prior quarter) due to premiumization (dairy, new launches) and discount cuts, despite pack upsizing.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aluminum can shortage constraining volume growth for energy drinks | Ballerino Glass Works (Unlisted) / Glass Packaging Suppliers | beneficiary | Low | Management noted switching to PET or glass if cans unavailable; however, PET is the primary substitute mentioned. |
| Input cost inflation (crude/packaging) hurting smaller players with lower inventory covers | Varun Beverages Limited | beneficiary | High | VBL's 6-month inventory cover in international markets and strong balance sheet allow it to outlast competitors who may blink first on pricing or volume. |
| Campa/Coke aggressive expansion potentially diluting market share | Smaller Regional Bottlers / Unorganized Water Players | loser | Med | VBL's scale, chilling infrastructure (1M+ visi-coolers), and ability to absorb costs via efficiency will likely squeeze out smaller, less efficient players. |

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Key player in the global beverage industry and the second largest franchisee of PepsiCo in the world (outside US) with franchise operations spanning across 10 countries and with distribution rights in additional 4 countries."
- "Symbiotic Relationship with PepsiCo": VBL owns Demand Delivery (production facilities, sales & distribution/GTM & logistics, in-outlet visi-coolers, BTL consumer push) while PepsiCo owns Demand Creation (trademarks, concentrate formulation, product/packaging R&D, ATL brand development).
- "34+ Years of Association (agreement in India valid till April, 2049)" and "90%+ of PepsiCo India Sales Volume".
- Franchise footprint: "VBL has been granted franchises for various PepsiCo products across 26 States and 6 Union Territories in India", plus Nepal, Sri Lanka, Morocco, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Lesotho, Eswatini & DRC, with distribution rights for Namibia, Botswana, Mozambique and Madagascar.
- "India is the largest market and contributed ~67% of revenues from operations (net) in Fiscal 2025."

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [PepsiCo EBA] "VBL and PepsiCo Inc. and its affiliates have entered into a revised Exclusive bottling appointment and trademark license agreement for India ('EBA') on May 21, 2026", with "(i) extension of the EBA term to April 30, 2049 (from April 30, 2039), and (ii) removal of the earlier restriction requiring VBL to operate solely as an SPV for PepsiCo's business, providing greater operational flexibility to explore, expand and avail benefits of scale and synergies."
- [Asahi/CALPIS] "On 18 June 2026, VBL has entered into a business alliance with Asahi Group Holdings to introduce and commercialize the CALPIS brand in India through a franchise arrangement"; CALPIS is "Japan's iconic fermented milk-based beverage brand with a legacy of over 100 years".
- [Kenya acquisition] "On 06 July 2026, VBL Industries (Kenya) Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of VBL has entered into a Business Transfer Agreement to acquire the business in DFIKL, a promoter group company, for a purchase consideration of USD 32 million (~INR 3,050 million, 1 USD = 95.30 INR) based upon the valuation of net assets from an independent third-party valuer."
- [Kenya acquisition] "DFIKL has net revenue of over Rs. 3,000 million for value added dairy, juices, packaged drinking water, etc. for the financial year ended March 2026. DFIKL also has an existing GTM infrastructure in place", and the deal "will provide us with the ready GTM in Kenya for expansion into carbonated soft drinks and energy drinks".
- [Snacks] Beyond beverages, VBL does "Manufacturing & Distribution of PepsiCo's snack foods in Morocco and Zimbabwe and distribution in Zambia; Co-manufacturing of Kurkure Puffcorn in India", and "Manufacturing & Distribution of own brands is restricted in select territories".
